children: Dutch consumer protection and digital rights organizations have approached a court in Amsterdam seeking to stop the sale of Meta Platforms’
smart glasses in the Netherlands, citing concerns over unauthorized recording and alleged breaches of European privacy regulations, Reuters reported on Thursday.

The action, brought by Consumentenbond and Offlimits, seeks restrictions on the use of footage captured through the devices, including a ban on using such recordings to develop AI models. The groups have also asked the court to suspend sales until the alleged violations are addressed. They are seeking financial penalties of up to €100,000 per day for each defendant, subject to a combined cap of €100 million.

has challenged the demands, arguing that product manufacturers should not be held accountable for intentional misuse by individual users. Its legal team also rejected claims that recordings made in Europe are processed or used to train AI systems, citing the indicator light on the glasses as a notification that recording is taking place.
manufacturing partner and Ray-Ban owner, told the court it has no access to the recorded footage.

The legal challenge follows growing international scrutiny of the devices. The Dutch privacy regulator recently advised consumers against purchasing them, while Germany's national consumer federation has initiated separate legal proceedings.

title: Meta’s AI glasses draw legal challenge from Dutch consumer bodies
